conviction_note: Net of five findings that genuinely cut both ways: the two concrete positives (a peer's dated evidence that tiered fuel surcharges recovered ~70% instead of the usual 30-40% at exactly these diesel levels, and $109m of a four-year repurchase authorisation from September 2022 still unused with leverage already below target) are worth more than the FY27 fuel/target-framing risk, which the -6.6% 20-day drift alongside the August diesel spike has already partly priced; against a 12% indicative implied move and a 10.2% median absolute reaction this is a small tilt, not a call.

findings.finding: US Foods' CFO said on 2026-08-13 that his fuel surcharge recovery rate ran "more like 70% for the quarter" versus "our typical 30%, 40%", turning an expected 2% fuel headwind into "less than half of that", explicitly because high diesel "triggered additional customer surcharges that normally only activate at elevated price levels" - the same tiered-surcharge mechanism UNFI described on 2026-06-09 as "contractual protection to share some of the fuel pressures with our customers", in a quarter that overlaps UNFI's 13 weeks to 2026-08-01.
findings.why_not_priced: Every published UNFI preview lists fuel as the downside risk and none of them mentions surcharge recovery. The 2026-09-03 stockpil preview names "incremental fuel and transportation costs" as risk #3 and assigns a 0.00% earnings surprise probability; if the surcharge-tier effect were priced, previews would be framing high diesel as margin-neutral-to-positive for a contracted wholesaler rather than as a pure cost, and UNFI would not have drifted -6.6% over the twenty days in which diesel made new highs. The read-through also requires the reader to have listened to a foodservice distributor's call to price a grocery wholesaler.
findings.independence: EIA weekly on-highway diesel shows UNFI's fiscal Q4 (13 weeks to 2026-08-01) averaged $5.18/gal against the $5.21 spot on the day the guide was set (2026-06-09), i.e. fuel did not worsen after guidance, with a mid-quarter low of $4.578 on 2026-07-06: https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=pet&s=emd_epd2d_pte_nus_dpg&f=w . Shares its subject (diesel) with finding 4 but the opposite time period and a different document.

findings.finding: UNFI's 2022 Repurchase Program - $200m authorised 2022-09-21 for a four-year term, so its term runs out this month - still had approximately $109m unused as of 2026-05-02, equal to about 4.2% of the $2.6bn market cap, while net leverage is already at 2.5x heading to ~2.3x against a stated <=2.5x-by-FY26 target and the last buys were struck at $33.66 (Q2) versus $43.94 spot.
findings.why_not_priced: No preview, no aggregator note and no analyst comment I could find mentions the authorisation expiring, and the fiscal-year-end print is the only board-meeting-adjacent event before the term lapses. If a new or upsized authorisation were priced, the coverage would be discussing capital-return capacity on a name whose own CEO has said the retail turnaround is "not part of our projections" - instead every published preview frames the print purely as revenue-decline-versus-margin-gain. The 5-day/-4.1% and 20-day/-6.6% drift into the print is the opposite of what a market anticipating a buyback announcement looks like.
findings.independence: Corroborated independently: an investing.com summary of the Q2 10-Q dated 2025-12-17 gives the same $200m-over-four-years structure with $138m then remaining and the company "expects to resume opportunistic repurchases" (https://www.investing.com/news/sec-filings/united-natural-foods-shareholders-approve-equity-plan-and-resume-buyback-program-93CH-4413714), and $138m less the $25m bought in Q2 (Q2 FY26 release) and $4m in Q3 (10-Q equity statement) reconciles exactly to $109m. Caveat: the authorisation-date/term sentence is quoted from the 10-Q as surfaced by full-text search - the rendered page truncates before that note.

findings.finding: The Q4 bar the wire will print at 6:30am - $7.6bn revenue, $0.62 adjusted EPS - is asymmetric against UNFI's own narrowed FY26 guide: $31.1-31.3bn sales less $23.51bn of 39-week actuals implies Q4 sales of $7.59-7.79bn, so $7.6bn sits at the floor of the guided band, whereas $2.40-2.60 adjusted EPS less $1.95 YTD implies Q4 of $0.45-0.65 and $0.62 sits at the ~85th percentile.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the exact inverse of the Q3 setup, where the Street's $7.96bn revenue estimate sat roughly $260m above the guide-implied ~$7.7bn and the stock fell 10.28% on a revenue miss with in-line EPS and +16.6% EBITDA. If the market had absorbed the lesson symmetrically, the previews would be flagging that the revenue bar has now been set below the company's own floor; instead they simply reprint $7.6bn/-1.6% with no guidance bridge. The two aggregators do not even agree - the FY-level consensus of $31.20bn implies $7.69bn for Q4, $90m above the quarterly consensus being quoted.
findings.independence: The $7.6bn/$0.62 bar is confirmed on a preview dated 2026-09-03 (https://stockpil.com/unfi-q4-earnings-preview-september-2026) and the FY-level $31.20bn/$2.56 nine-analyst set on https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/unfi/forecast/ ; note this finding draws its guidance ranges from the same 2026-06-09 8-K exhibit as finding 4, so the two should not be counted as independent documents.

findings.finding: The first FY27 guide has to be set against a fuel base far above FY26's with only partial hedging, and UNFI's own multi-year frame gives it cover to guide flat: EIA weekly diesel was $5.599/gal on 2026-08-31 versus $3.708 a year earlier (+51%), the fiscal-Q1-to-date August average is $5.46 versus $3.74 (+46%), and against FY24 adjusted EBITDA of $518m the published "low-double-digit average annual Adjusted EBITDA growth from FY24 to FY27" target is satisfied by FY27 of roughly $690-730m - i.e. flat to +5% on the FY26 guide midpoint of $695m - even though the longer-term algorithm management talks to is high-single-digit EBITDA growth.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced - the -6.6% twenty-day drift coincides with the August diesel run - which is why I have haircut it. What is not priced is the target arithmetic: nobody has published the FY24 $518m base against the FY24-FY27 CAGR target to show that management's headline multi-year promise is already met by a flat FY27, so the Street's FY27 models anchor on the high-single-digit algorithm (~$750m) rather than on the ~$700m the stated target actually obliges. If that had been done, the sell-side FY27 EBITDA distribution would be visibly bimodal and the previews would lead with FY27 rather than with Q4 revenue.
findings.independence: Sysco's FY2026 10-K, filed August 2026, discloses diesel swaps covering ~87m gallons through June 2028 that lock roughly 80% of bulk fuel purchases for fiscal 2027 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000096021/000009602126000033/syy-20260627.htm) whereas UNFI said only that it hedges "parts of the fuel" on 2026-06-09 - so the nearest large peer entered FY27 hedged and UNFI did not. The FY24 $518m base is from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000102085924000040/f24q4earningsrelease.htm (2024-10-01) and the FY24-FY27 target language from https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/unfi-q4-2025-slides-cyber-incident-impacts-results-company-raises-longterm-targets-93CH-4263024 (2025-09-30).

findings.finding: The executive who will deliver UNFI's first FY27 guidance started five weeks ago: the 2026-07-09 8-K appointed Alfredo Luchini CFO effective 2026-08-10 (from Carrier Climate Solutions Americas), moved Matteo Tarditi from President/CFO to President/COO, elevated Louis Martin to Chief Commercial Officer and disclosed Mark Bushway's exit - and a fifth change, Matt Echols ceasing to be Chief Corporate Affairs Officer effective 2026-08-24, was disclosed only in a Form 4 remark filed 2026-08-27, with no Item 5.02 8-K, no press release and no trade-press coverage.
findings.why_not_priced: The July reshuffle was covered by trade press, but the Echols exit was not - a search on his name and title returns only the 2022 appointment release and July 2026 leadership stories that still list him, and UNFI's own executive-management page has dropped him. More to the point, no preview draws the operational conclusion: an incoming CFO setting a maiden full-year range typically widens it and anchors low, which matters disproportionately here because the FY27 range is the event. If this were priced the option skew would exist and be positive; the baseline has no 25-delta skew at all and 1,765 contracts of front-expiry open interest, so no one has expressed a directional view on guide-setting risk.
findings.independence: UNFI's own governance page now lists eight executives and Echols is absent while Luchini appears as CFO (https://ir.unfi.com/governance/executive-management/default.aspx), and the Form 4 accepted 2026-08-27 carries no transactions - only the cessation remark (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000162828026059263/wk-form4_1787862228.xml). Mildly self-limiting: Tarditi, who built the FY26 guidance framework, is still in the building as President/COO, which is why I have kept this small.

searched_and_found_nothing: Whole Foods / Amazon customer-concentration renewal risk - the distribution agreement was amended and restated on 2024-05-21 and runs to 2032-05-20 per the FY24 10-K, so there is no near-term renewal event and nothing new since 2026-06-09

Retail / Cub Foods divestiture closing - no 8-K asset-sale closing between 2026-06-09 and 2026-09-04; the only development is three Cub stores to franchisee Jerry's Enterprises (Grocery Dive, 2026-08-17) framed as strengthening rather than exiting Cub, with no disclosed close date or proceeds

FY27 pre-framing since the Q3 call - no investor conference, business update, 8-K investor deck or fireside chat between 2026-06-09 and 2026-09-04; the only 8-Ks are the 2026-06-22 term-loan repricing and the 2026-07-09 leadership item

Credit-agreement covenant relief - Term Loan Amendment No. 5 (2026-06-18) only repriced ~$371m from SOFR+4.75% to SOFR+4.00%, expressly leaving all other material terms unchanged; ~$2.8m of annual interest saving and already carried by StockTitan/TipRanks/TradingView, so priced and immaterial

New WARN notices or DC closures in the Jun-Sep 2026 window - only the March 2026 Sturtevant WI filing (443 separations phased 2026-06-20 to 2026-08-01, volume to Joliet IL), which pre-dates the last print
Labour action - the Pompano Beach FL Teamsters strike authorisation was resolved by a ratified five-year contract in April 2026; nothing new since

Natural-channel demand read-through was too weak to size: Natural Grocers' quarter to 2026-06-30 accelerated to +1.2% daily average comps from +0.5% (2026-08-06) while Sprouts ran -1.0% comps for the June quarter (2026-07-29) - directionally offsetting
Food-at-home CPI was +2.7% y/y in July 2026 and flat m/m, i.e. no inflation inflection to change the wholesale dollar-sales trajectory
Insider Form 4/144 cluster - could not render openinsider or the individual June 2026 Form 4 index pages (SEC 503s); no conclusion drawn

Sell-side coverage staleness - the screen's 'only 2 estimates' premise did not hold up: stockanalysis shows nine analysts on FY26 with a $49.38 average target, so the consensus is not two stale numbers
baseline_tension: The baseline offers no direction (no 25-delta skew, 1,765 contracts of open interest, 39%-of-mid ATM spread) and a negative run-up, and my net is mildly against that drift - the two positives rest on documents nobody reads for UNFI (a foodservice peer's surcharge-recovery quote and an expiring buyback authorisation) while the FY27 fuel risk that most plausibly explains the -6.6% twenty-day drift is the one finding I have deliberately haircut as partly priced.
